clue.text: Fictional duke captured by actors in Othello

indicators.note: captured by means held inside, so the name sits within the letters of actors in Othello

explanation.surface: A fictional duke played by the cast of Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Orsino is the Duke of Illyria in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, a character from fiction.

clue.text: City still jubilant

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
still means motionless, static

explanation.surface: The City remains jubilant, perhaps after good market news.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic means overjoyed, a near synonym of jubilant.

clue.text: Hauls associated with amended awful weapon

parts.note: winches as a verb means hauls with a winding machine

indicators.note: amended means changed slightly, here one letter of the awful word swapped for another

parts.note: awful means terrible

explanation.surface: Hauls of guns go with an awful, freshly altered weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amended' changes the B of TERRIBLE to F, giving TERRIFLE; the clue does not say which letters, so the answer must guide it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Winchester was a famous American lever-action repeating rifle, a firearm or weapon.

clue.text: Succeed because of their supply

parts.note: in can mean because of, as in 'in consequence of'

indicators.note: supply read as supplely, bendily, so the letters of their are rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm prospers on the strength of its suppliers' goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed someone is to follow them into a title or estate, which is to inherit it.

clue.text: Horrid deflating creeps belittling themselves

indicators.note: horrid means nasty or disordered, so the letters of deflating creeps are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nasty, deflating creeps who run themselves down.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-deprecating describes people who play down their own worth, modestly belittling themselves.

clue.text: Force needed to enter unopened, rubbish shed

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside, so the force letter goes within the trimmed rubbish word
unopened means the first letter is removed

parts.note: refuse means rubbish
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: Force was needed to get into a shed full of unopened rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' strips the R from REFUSE, leaving EFUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To effuse is to pour out or give off, so to shed liquid or light.

clue.text: Big guns planning to sack international

indicators.note: to sack means to dismiss, so one letter is thrown out

parts.note: ordinance once meant ordering or arrangement, a planning

explanation.surface: The big guns of a company are planning to fire an international colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: Big guns at first reads as bosses; here it is literal artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance means artillery, the heavy guns of an army.

clue.text: Lie about Romeo in disagreement

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for a lie is wrapped around the letter

parts.note: a lie is a fiction, an invented story
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone tells a tall story about Romeo during a quarrel, perhaps among actors or critics.
explanation.definitionFit: Friction between people is conflict or clashing, a synonym for disagreement.

clue.text: Anything made in France beneficial to stopping European market's closure

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so these pieces go inside the outer pair
closure means the end, so only the final letter of market is taken

parts.note: the possessive just reads as market
F is the international vehicle code for France
something good for you is beneficial to you

explanation.surface: Talk of goods made in France helping to keep a European market from closing down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopping' puts F and FOR between E and T, the last letter of 'market's' read as market.
explanation.definitionFit: An effort can be a thing produced, as in 'the novel is her best effort', so loosely anything made.

clue.text: Possibly punchy first line in Liverpool, for example

indicators.note: in places the first-plus-line letters within the club abbreviation

parts.note: Liverpool is a football club, abbreviated FC
1st is written IST in letters
a straight vertical line looks like the letter I

explanation.surface: A boxer-like first line in a Liverpool song, perhaps, might be called punchy.
explanation.walkthrough: IST comes from writing 1st with I for the digit 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Fistic means to do with boxing or fisticuffs, so possibly punchy in the fighting sense.

clue.text: Graceful after only hints of excuse for discharge

indicators.note: after puts the word for graceful behind the two initials
a hint is just a trace, so only each word's first letter is used

parts.note: graceful movement or speech is fluent, smooth and flowing

explanation.surface: Someone graceful offers only a hint of an excuse for being dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: Effluent is liquid waste let out from a factory or sewer, a discharge.

clue.text: Temporarily staying in position after me fortieth shot

indicators.note: after puts the staying-in-position word behind the rearranged letters
shot means ruined or broken, so the letters of me fortieth are rearranged

parts.note: to be can mean to stay put, as in 'let it be'

explanation.surface: Someone stays put, for now, after a fortieth attempt at something.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means for now or for the present, which is what temporarily expresses.

clue.text: One side of Manchester chasing money for profitable conditions

indicators.note: chasing means coming behind, so the Manchester club follows the money word

parts.note: fat is slang for money or surplus profit
Manchester City is one of the city's two football sides, the other being United

explanation.surface: A football club from Manchester chasing cash, which promises lucrative times.
explanation.definitionFit: Fat city is American slang for a state of prosperity, the comfortable conditions of a big profit.

clue.text: Unusually arcane about Greek lyric poet

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of arcane in an odd order

parts.note: on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: An unusually obscure verse about a Greek lyric poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Anacreon was an ancient Greek lyric poet known for drinking songs.

clue.text: Doctor following writer

parts.note: following means coming after

explanation.surface: A doctor follows a writer, perhaps a stalker in a thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: A drafter is one who draws up documents, so a writer of drafts.

clue.text: One cutting crewman who keeps members up? More like down

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the numeral letter goes inside the crewman

parts.note: a fluffer is a film-set crew member whose job keeps male actors aroused
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A crewman who keeps union members on side, cut, as the mood goes down.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is soft fine feathers, so something more like down is softer and fluffier.

clue.text: Composition of Chopin's evoked science of sound

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters of Chopin's are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A Chopin piece calls to mind the science of sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Phonics is an old name for acoustics, the study of sound, as well as a reading method.

clue.text: Fancy treacherous prof getting what one expected?

indicators.note: fancy as a verb hints at elaborate reworking, so the letters of treacherous prof are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fancy that: a treacherous professor got exactly what one would have predicted.
explanation.definitionFit: The golf idiom means normal and to be expected, as a par score is the standard for a course.

clue.text: Views temperature dials going round

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the dial word wraps the temperature letter

parts.note: dials is slang for faces

explanation.surface: Temperature dials spin round, from different points of view.
explanation.definitionFit: Facets of a matter are its aspects, its different views or angles.

clue.text: Floozie hot about introduction to Endeavour Morse, perhaps

indicators.note: about means going round, so the floozie-and-hot letters wrap the initial

parts.note: floozie and slut are both disparaging words for a promiscuous woman

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so only the first letter of Endeavour is taken

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A hot floozie appears early in an episode of a TV detective series.
explanation.walkthrough: Endeavour Morse is the Oxford detective of the British TV series Inspector Morse and its prequel Endeavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Morse is a fictional detective, an example of a sleuth.

clue.text: A bit of fighting on Friday

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the fighting word comes behind the day abbreviation

parts.note: action is military fighting, as in 'killed in action'

explanation.surface: A little fighting broke out on Friday night.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraction is a small part of something, so a bit.

clue.text: Caught hard old hooligan sporting a goatee?

indicators.note: caught means heard, so a word is given by how it sounds

parts.note: hard means tough
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress, often seen as a thug

explanation.surface: A tough old thug arrested, and he had a little beard on his chin.
explanation.walkthrough: TOUGH said out loud gives TUF.
explanation.definitionFit: Tufted means bearing a tuft, and a goatee is a tuft of hair on the chin, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Some diplomats and others like what's yet to be delivered?

definitions.text: like what's yet to be delivered?

parts.note: the FO, Foreign Office, is the British diplomatic service
et al is Latin shorthand for and others

explanation.surface: Some diplomats and their colleagues are like a parcel still awaiting delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: Foetal means relating to an unborn baby, one yet to be delivered by midwife or doctor.

clue.text: Paper coverage offered to recently inaugurated union members

definitions.text: Paper coverage offered to recently inaugurated union members

parts.words: Paper coverage offered to recently inaugurated union members
parts.note: the surface suggests press coverage of new trade-union members; the real union is a marriage and its newly-weds get showered in paper scraps
